findings.desc: verificationIntent/checklist requires all actionable recommendation classes to be classified, including recommend_demote, but playbook-promotion-observe-smoke and recorded verificationEvidence cover recommend_activate, reject, archive, mark_non_deducible, and hold only. Add an explicit recommend_demote handled/unhandled observation case so the actionable-class contract is covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Added explicit recommend_demote smoke coverage proving active demote recommendations remain unhandled while still active and become handled after status changes away from active. Verified by npm --prefix packages/main run build and node packages/main/dist/tasks/playbook-promotion-observe-smoke.js (11/11 pass).

findings.desc: playbook_promotion_observe treats an archive recommendation as handled when the current playbook status is still stale. The evaluator emits action="archive" specifically when aggregate.status === "stale" (learning-store.ts:1121-1125), but classifyRecommendationHandling returns handled/current_status_stale for row.action === "archive" or "reject" (learning-store.ts:1493-1502). That makes a newly applied archive recommendation disappear from unhandled backlog without any archive transition or archived metadata being present; the smoke test encodes this optimistic case at playbook-promotion-observe-smoke.ts:297-317. Archive should remain unhandled while current status is stale, and only become handled when current status/metadata actually records archived (or whatever explicit archive sink is chosen).

CHK-001 userSees requires JSON/text output to include candidateConsumed.unconsumedCurrentCandidateIds, but the report contract only exposes consumedCandidateCount/count/uniquePlaybookCount/malformedOutcomeRows/excluded/rows (experience-layer-types.ts:406-416), buildPlaybookPromotionObserveReport returns the same shape without computing current candidates minus consumed ids (learning-store.ts:1624-1645), and the text renderer has no candidateConsumed.unconsumedCurrentCandidateIds line (handlers/playbook.ts:569-577). This misses the stated output needed to identify current candidates that exist but have no explicit consumption row.

Concept blocker: CHK-001 promises candidateConsumed.unconsumedCurrentCandidateIds so the observe surface directly answers which current candidates are not being consumed before M7/M8 automation. The implemented report type only exposes consumedCandidateCount/count/uniquePlaybookCount/excluded/rows (experience-layer-types.ts:406-417), buildPlaybookPromotionObserveReport returns only those fields (learning-store.ts:1634-1645), and text output renders only counts/rows (handlers/playbook.ts:569-577). Users can infer a backlog by diffing candidateGenerated.candidates against rows, but the command does not provide the explicit current-candidate backlog signal required by the story.
